best_human.source: Erdos and Fishburn (1996), Table 1, triangular lattice, s=6, n=91
best_human.evidence_state: coordinate construction reconstructed and exact score independently verified

best_public.source: Erdos and Fishburn (1996), Table 1; best same-parameter explicit result found in the sources checked
best_public.evidence_state: reported construction reproduced from its formula; not a proof of optimality

best_reproduced.evidence_state: exact field arithmetic verifies 91 distinct points and 34 distinct squared distances

known_lower_bound.meaning: Erdos 1946, Theorem 1: n-1 <= k(k+1) when k distinct distances are determined; for n=91, 90 <= k(k+1), so k >= 9

limitations: The 34-distance construction is an upper bound on the minimum, not an exact optimum result.
The literature check did not locate an exact value for n=91; this survey is not exhaustive.
The checker handles exact real algebraic coordinates. Candidate programs that output only floating-point coordinates are invalid.
